_about: EG's games table (Nov 17, 2026): every game named as an example in definitions.json, plus the games the LL has in hand in week 11. Fields follow ../format.md v1.0 (Games). year, designer and definition come from the sources listed; where sources is empty they are EG's from general knowledge and not yet checked. inTheLL entries cite the LL's record. build.mjs adds each game's mechanics from the examples.

games.name: Data Center
games.designer: The LL (GL, Claude Code), for week 11
games.whereToGet: http://localhost:3111/game/play/data-center (the week's reader app, on the laptop)
games.definition: The week 11 game: an AI spreads across a region's infrastructure while four human factions (the utility, the city council, the company, the neighbors) act in turn, each with a private goal; one hidden card in the AI's deck is the turn.

inTheLL.text: Built Nov 14, 2026, for TDM 155AI on Nov 18 and William Stafford's SOC-STD 98to workshop on Nov 23.

games.howTo: Run the reader app (`pnpm dev` in `nextjs/`) and open `/game/play/data-center`; four players or teams share one screen. `/game/edit/data-center` opens the rules for a remix.

games.name: Normal Technology
games.designer: The LL (GL, Claude Code), for week 11
games.definition: The Data Center map rewritten after Narayanan and Kapoor's 'AI as Normal Technology': the AI spreads only where someone approves or signs a deal, every site pays something back, and there is no turn.

inTheLL.text: Built Nov 14, 2026, to play after Data Center and compare the claims.

games.howTo: Open `/game/play/normal-technology` in the reader app, after a round of Data Center.

games.name: The Committee
games.designer: The LL (GL, Claude Code), for week 11
games.definition: A version of the week 11 game in which the AI brings proposals to one oversight committee; the players rename its goal before playing.

inTheLL.text: Built Nov 14, 2026 (option A of the design notes).

games.name: Blank
games.designer: The LL (GL, Claude Code), for week 11
games.definition: The week 11 game's empty starting point: three places, one card, one faction, one action, for students who build a game from scratch.

inTheLL.text: Built Nov 14, 2026, for remixing from scratch.

games.howTo: Open `/game/edit/blank` and add to it, or ask Claude Code to change `_content/game/_rulesets/blank.json`.

games.name: Universal Paperclips
games.definition: Frank Lantz's 2017 browser game, in which the player is an AI that makes paperclips until there is nothing left.

inTheLL.text: The starting point for the week 11 game and for William Stafford's Nov 23 workshop (Nov 2026).
Modeled as data on the week 11 game-state pages (Nov 14, 2026).

games.name: Monopoly
games.definition: A board game of buying property around a loop of forty spaces and charging rent, until all but one player is bankrupt.

inTheLL.text: Modeled as data on the week 11 game-state pages (Nov 14, 2026), from overhead photos of a game in progress, for TDM 155AI.
The LL's own Monopoly set is the table for the prototype 'Monopoly with live rents' (Nov 15, 2026).

games.name: Risk
games.definition: A board game of world conquest on a map of 42 territories in six continents, with battles decided by dice.

inTheLL.text: Modeled as data on the week 11 game-state pages (Nov 14, 2026).

games.name: The Game of Life
games.definition: A board game along one branching track of a life (college or career, marriage, family, retirement), moved by a spinner from 1 to 10.

inTheLL.text: Modeled as data on the week 11 game-state pages (Nov 14, 2026).
Named in the ENGL 189VG planning for the difference between rolling dice and spinning a spinner (fall 2026).

games.name: Texas Hold'em
games.definition: A poker game in which each player holds two hole cards face down and shares five community cards, betting over four rounds.

inTheLL.text: Modeled as data on the week 11 game-state pages (Nov 14, 2026).

games.name: Civilization
games.definition: A turn-based strategy series in which the player leads a civilization from its first city through history, exploring, expanding, exploiting and exterminating (4X).

inTheLL.text: Modeled as data on the week 11 game-state pages (Nov 14, 2026), from Civilization V–VII's game definitions.

games.name: Dungeons & Dragons
games.definition: A tabletop role-playing game in which players voice characters in a story run by a dungeon master, with dice deciding what their actions achieve.

inTheLL.text: Named in the ENGL 189VG brainstorm as an example of loops and of open-world play (fall 2026).

games.name: League of Legends
games.definition: A team game (a multiplayer online battle arena) in which two teams of five champions fight to destroy each other's base.

inTheLL.text: Named in the ENGL 189VG brainstorm as an example of a loop (fall 2026).

games.name: Baldur's Gate (series)
games.designer: BioWare; Baldur's Gate 3 (2023) by Larian Studios
games.definition: A series of role-playing video games set in the Dungeons & Dragons world, in which the player leads a party whose conversations and choices shape the story.

inTheLL.text: Named in the ENGL 189VG brainstorm as an example of open-world narrative (fall 2026; the note does not say which game in the series).

games.name: Final Fantasy X
games.definition: A Japanese role-playing game in which a party travels a world fighting in turn-based battles to defeat a recurring monster, Sin.

inTheLL.text: Named in the ENGL 189VG brainstorm for endings unlocked by exploration (fall 2026).

games.name: God of War (2018)
games.definition: An action game in which Kratos and his son cross a Norse world; Kratos's main weapon, the Leviathan Axe, can be thrown and recalled.

inTheLL.text: Named in the ENGL 189VG planning as a close-reading example: 'god of war axe mechanic' (fall 2026; the note does not name the game's year, and the axe is the 2018 game's).

games.name: The Legend of Zelda
games.definition: An action-adventure game in which Link explores an overworld and dungeons room by room, gathering items that open new areas.

inTheLL.text: Named in the ENGL 189VG vibe-coding station notes ('old-zelda-like room based system') as a model for a simple vibe-coded game (fall 2026).

games.name: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild
games.definition: An open-world Zelda game in which the player can go almost anywhere from the start and solve problems with physics and chemistry systems.

inTheLL.text: Marlon's example of template and instance (every horse has the same properties; yours is an instance), Nov 14, 2026.

games.name: Chess
games.definition: A two-player game on a board of 64 squares, in which each side tries to checkmate the other's king.

inTheLL.text: Nov 16, 2026: the first test of computer vision that reads game boards in the studio started with chess (Marlon's day-one report, voice agent's record).

games.name: Go
games.definition: A two-player game of placing stones on a 19x19 grid to surround territory.

games.name: Pandemic
games.definition: A cooperative board game in which players with different roles travel the world treating outbreaks and racing to cure four diseases.

games.name: Pandemic Legacy: Season 1
games.designer: Rob Daviau and Matt Leacock (Z-Man Games)
games.definition: A campaign version of Pandemic played over a year of game months, in which the board and cards are changed for good after each game.

games.name: Catan
games.definition: A board game of settling an island of hexes, collecting resources by dice roll and trading them to build roads, settlements and cities.

games.name: Dominion
games.definition: The first deck-building card game: players buy cards from a shared supply into their own decks, aiming for the most victory points.

games.name: Slay the Spire
games.definition: A single-player game that combines deck-building with a roguelike climb, fighting with the cards you collect.

games.name: Hanabi
games.definition: A cooperative card game in which players hold their cards facing out and give each other limited hints to build fireworks in order.

games.name: Puerto Rico
games.definition: A board game of running a colonial plantation economy, in which players take roles in turn each round.

games.name: Werewolf (Mafia)
games.designer: Dmitry Davidoff (Mafia); Werewolf variant by Andrew Plotkin
games.definition: A party game of hidden roles in which a village votes each day to eliminate a suspect, while werewolves secretly kill at night.

games.name: Quiplash
games.definition: A party game played on phones in which players write funny answers to prompts and everyone votes between pairs of answers.

games.name: Stratego
games.definition: A two-player game of capturing the flag, in which each piece's rank is hidden from the opponent.

games.name: Battlestar Galactica: The Board Game
games.definition: A semi-cooperative board game in which humans flee the Cylons, while one or more players are secretly Cylons working against them.

games.name: Yahtzee
games.designer: E. S. Lowe; later Milton Bradley
games.definition: A dice game of rolling five dice up to three times a turn to make scoring combinations.

games.name: Boggle
games.definition: A word game in which players find words in a grid of lettered dice before a sand timer runs out.

games.name: Scrabble
games.definition: A word game of placing lettered tiles on a grid to make words, scored by letter values and premium squares.

games.name: Pac-Man
games.definition: An arcade game in which the player eats dots in a maze while four ghosts chase them.

games.name: Tetris
games.definition: A puzzle game in which falling pieces of four squares are turned and placed to clear full lines.

games.name: Space Invaders
games.definition: An arcade game in which the player's cannon shoots rows of descending aliens.

games.name: Cookie Clicker
games.definition: An incremental browser game in which clicking a cookie, then buying buildings that bake for you, makes ever larger numbers of cookies.

games.name: The Oregon Trail
games.designer: Don Rawitsch, Bill Heinemann and Paul Dillenberger (MECC)
games.definition: An educational game in which a party of settlers travels the trail from Missouri to Oregon in 1847, managing supplies through random hardships.

games.name: Mass Effect
games.definition: A science-fiction role-playing game in which the player's dialogue choices and decisions carry across a trilogy.

games.name: Frostpunk
games.definition: A city-building survival game in which the player runs the last city in a frozen world, passing laws that keep people alive at a cost.

games.name: McDonald's Video Game
games.definition: A satirical browser game in which the player runs a fast-food corporation from pasture to restaurant to boardroom.

games.name: Fishbanks
games.definition: A role-play simulation in which teams run fishing companies sharing one fish stock, used to teach the management of common resources.

games.name: Skylanders: Spyro's Adventure
games.definition: A video game played by placing toy figures on a 'Portal of Power' connected to the console, which brings each figure's character into the game.

games.name: Fluxx
games.definition: A card game whose rules and goal change as cards are played.

games.name: Pokémon Red and Blue
games.definition: A role-playing game in which the player catches and trains creatures and fights turn-based battles.

games.name: Super Mario Bros.
games.definition: A side-scrolling platform game in which Mario runs and jumps through levels to rescue a princess.

games.name: Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes
games.definition: A cooperative game in which one player defuses a bomb on screen while the others read the defusal manual aloud.

games.name: Dark Souls
games.definition: An action role-playing game set in a decaying kingdom of interconnected areas, known for its difficulty.

games.name: Portal
games.definition: A first-person puzzle game in which the player solves test chambers with a gun that makes linked portals.

games.name: Undertale
games.definition: A role-playing game in which the player can spare every monster instead of fighting it.

games.name: Final Fantasy X-2
games.definition: The sequel to Final Fantasy X, with mission-based play and several endings that depend on how much the player completed.

games.name: Papers, Please
games.definition: A game in which the player is an immigration inspector in a fictional authoritarian state, checking documents at a border crossing.

games.name: Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons
games.definition: An adventure game in which one player steers two brothers at once, one on each half of the controller.

games.name: Animal Crossing
games.definition: A life-simulation game in which the player lives in a village of animals and pays off a house loan to the shopkeeper Tom Nook.

games.name: The Sims
games.definition: A life-simulation game in which the player creates people and directs their daily lives in a house.

games.name: Wii Sports
games.definition: A collection of sports games played by swinging the Wii Remote.

games.name: Guitar Hero
games.definition: A rhythm game played on a guitar-shaped controller, pressing colored frets and strumming in time to songs.

games.name: Hades
games.definition: A roguelike action game in which Zagreus tries again and again to escape the underworld.

games.name: Overcooked!
games.definition: A cooperative cooking game in which players prepare and serve orders in chaotic kitchens against a clock.

games.name: Dance Dance Revolution
games.definition: A rhythm game played by stepping on arrows on a dance pad in time to music.

games.name: Can't Stop
games.definition: A dice game of pushing your luck up columns numbered 2 to 12.

games.name: Blackjack
games.definition: A casino card game in which players try to get closer to 21 than the dealer without going over.

games.name: Among Us
games.definition: A social deduction game in which crewmates try to find the impostors among them.

games.name: Zendo
games.definition: A game of inductive logic in which players discover a secret rule by building arrangements of pieces.

games.name: Diplomacy
games.definition: A strategy game of pre-First World War Europe with no dice, in which players negotiate and then move at the same time.

games.name: Twitch Plays Pokémon
games.definition: A 2014 stream in which viewers played Pokémon Red together by typing commands in the chat.

games.name: Once Upon a Time
games.designer: Richard Lambert, Andrew Rilstone and James Wallis (Atlas Games)
games.definition: A storytelling card game in which players tell a fairy tale together, each aiming for their own ending.

games.name: Simon Says
games.definition: A children's game in which players obey commands only when they begin 'Simon says'.

games.name: Just Dance
games.definition: A dance game in which players copy an on-screen dancer's moves.

games.name: Splendor
games.definition: A card game of collecting gems to buy development cards that discount later purchases.

games.name: Agricola
games.definition: A worker-placement game about running a seventeenth-century farm.

games.name: Minecraft
games.definition: A sandbox game of mining, gathering and building in a world of blocks.

games.name: Infinite Craft
games.definition: A browser game of combining elements into new ones, with results decided by a language model.

games.name: Twister
games.designer: Charles Foley and Neil Rabens (Milton Bradley)
games.definition: A physical game in which players place hands and feet on colored circles named by a spinner.

games.name: Pokémon Go
games.definition: A location-based phone game in which players catch creatures at real-world places.

games.name: Simon
games.designer: Ralph Baer and Howard Morrison (Milton Bradley)
games.definition: An electronic memory toy that plays growing sequences of lights and tones for the player to repeat.

games.name: Marco Polo
games.definition: A tag game played in a pool, in which the seeker keeps their eyes closed.

games.name: Pictionary
games.definition: A word-guessing game played by drawing.

games.name: Taboo
games.definition: A word-guessing game in which the clue-giver may not say the word or the listed related words.

games.name: Twenty Questions
games.definition: A guessing game of identifying something with no more than twenty yes-or-no questions.

games.name: Braid
games.definition: A puzzle platformer built around rewinding time.

games.name: Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time
games.definition: An action-adventure game in which a dagger lets the prince rewind time.

games.name: Façade
games.definition: An interactive drama in which the player types to a couple whose marriage is falling apart.

games.name: AI Dungeon
games.definition: A text adventure narrated by a language model in response to whatever the player types.

games.name: Peggle
games.definition: A puzzle game of shooting a ball to clear orange pegs from a board.

games.name: Cow Clicker
games.definition: Ian Bogost's satirical Facebook game, in which players click a cow every six hours.

games.name: Nomic
games.definition: A game in which changing the rules is the move.

games.name: Dead of Winter
games.designer: Jonathan Gilmour and Isaac Vega (Plaid Hat Games)
games.definition: A semi-cooperative survival game in which each player also has a secret objective.

games.name: Grow-a-Game
games.definition: A card deck of values, verbs, games and issues used as prompts for designing games.

games.name: Left 4 Dead
games.definition: A cooperative zombie shooter whose AI Director adjusts the game to the players.

games.name: Middle-earth: Shadow of Mordor
games.definition: An action game set in Mordor, known for its Nemesis system of orc captains who remember the player.

games.name: System Shock
games.definition: A first-person game aboard a space station run by a hostile AI, SHODAN.

games.name: The Talos Principle
games.definition: A first-person puzzle game in which a voice called Elohim gives the player commands.

games.name: Wordle
games.definition: A daily word game in which everyone guesses the same five-letter word in six tries.

games.name: Foldit
games.definition: A puzzle game in which players fold proteins.

games.name: Hole in the Wall
games.definition: A Kinect game, based on the American TV game show (itself adapted from Japan's Brain Wall), in which players fit their bodies through cut-out shapes in an approaching wall.

games.name: Wii Fit
games.definition: An exercise game played on the Balance Board, with yoga, strength, aerobics and balance activities.

games.name: EyeToy: Play
games.definition: A collection of minigames for the PlayStation 2's EyeToy camera, played by moving in front of it.

games.name: Fruit Ninja Kinect
games.definition: A Kinect version of Fruit Ninja in which the player slices thrown fruit with their arms.

games.name: King of the hill
games.definition: A children's game in which one player holds a hill or mound and the others try to knock them off it.
